 Centuries by Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder have lifted South Africa back into series contention against Australia on day four of the deciding Cape Town cricket test. South Africa began the day only 40 runs ahead and four wickets down. But a compelling fightback led by wicketkeeper Rickelton's 101 and allrounder Mulder's 115 has earned them a lead of 287. Mulder’s dismissal in the day’s last over ended South Africa’s second innings at 387. That's set Australia the entire fifth day to score 288 to win the series which is tied at 1-1. Australia pacer Mitchell Starc has taken 3-65 and a match haul of nine wickets.

 CAPE TOWN, South Africa (AP) — Centuries by Ryan Rickelton and Wiaan Mulder lifted South Africa back into series contention against Australia on a day of batting domination in the deciding Newlands cricket test on Friday.
 South Africa began day four only 40 runs ahead and four wickets down. But a compelling fightback led by wicketkeeper Rickelton, 101 off 219 balls, and allrounder Mulder, 115 off 221 balls, earned them a lead of 287.
